fi.stroomdiagrammengwt.client

    Package Description
    fi.stroomdiagrammengwt.client  
  • Classes in fi.stroomdiagrammengwt.client used by fi.stroomdiagrammengwt.client 
    Class and Description
    CapacityPanel
    class displaying the capacity of an edge as a box on the edge
    DiagramCopy
    a class containing the attributes of a flow diagram
    DiagramManager
    the class managing the layout of the flow diagram, in particular after inserting a vertex or deleting edges;
    the flow diagram is shown from left (where the root(s) are) to right with the vertices positioned from top to bottom in vertical layers
    it also saves the flow diagram in a DiagramCopy for getState and recreates a flow diagram from a DiagramCopy for setState and for the launchData
    Dimension
    there is no class Dimension in JavaGWT
    DrawingPanel
    class for drawing the flow diagram on a Canvas using its Context 2d;
    the layout of the flow diagram is handled by class DiagramManager;
    this class also processes the following Mouse/TouchEvents on the Canvas:
    clicking on the traceBack and addEdge buttons of a non-root vertex
    clicking and dragging a vertex (not on the buttons)
    clicking on the addEdge button of a root
    double or long click (not on the button) of a root to open a popup for flow input
    double or long click on the label of any vertex (if there are labels) to open a popup for label input
    double or long click on the capacityField of an edge to open a popup for capacity input;
    long click on an edge to delete it (if allowed, see class Edge)
    this class also takes care of tracing back flows and the user flow diagram history; the flow diagram history is NOT saved in getState/setState;
    tracing back flows: given a vertex, highlight all edges that contribute to the flow through this vertex;
    displaying edge thickness:
    relative: the sum of the vertical thicknesses of all edges out of a vertex equals the height of the vertex (excluding label) and the individual vertical thicknesses are proportional to the capacities of the edges
    absolute: the sum of the vertical thicknesses of all edges out of a root are displayed as in mode relative, for edges out of other vertices sum of the vertical thicknesses is proportional to the fraction (flow in vertex divided by maximum flow in the roots connected to the vertex).
    Edge
    class representing an edge in the flow diagram;
    each edge has a capacity, a number between 0 and 1;
    the sum of the capacities of the edges out of a vertex equals 1;
    the capacity is shown in the capacity field, a box drawn on the edge, see class CapacityField, and can be changed by doubleClick or longClick on the capacity field;
    when changing the capacity of an edge, the sum the sum of the capacities from all edges out of fromVertex of that edge is maintained at 1 by altering the capacity of the out edge that was set the longest time ago;
    the user can enter the capacity in another format then the global format in which case all the capacities of the edges out of fromVertex are displayed in this local format, e.g. one can enter a fraction while the global format is a decimal number;
    the edge can be deleted by longClick on the edge polygon outside the capacity field and this is allowed if:
    1) the toVertex of this edge has other incoming edges than this edge
    2) the toVertex of this edge has only this edge as incoming edge and has no outgoing edges; in this case the toVertex is also deleted;
    see class DrawingPanel for Mouse/Touch action and class EdgePopup for changing the capacity;
    capacities can be entered as decimal fractions, fractions or percentages.
    EdgeCopy
    class containing basic attributes of an edge
    LWArrowButton
    class simulating an up/right/down/left arrow button
    Point
    there is no class Point in JavaGWT
    Polygon
    there is no class Polygon in JavaGWT
    Rational
    class implementing fractions and their arithmetic
    Rectangle
    there is no class Rectangle in JavaGWT
    StroomDiagrammenGWT
    main class for StroomDiagrammenGWT
    the flow diagram consist of Vertices (class Vertex) and Edges (class edge);
    the flow diagram is drawn by class DrawingPanel, which contains a Canvas, while the layout is handled by class DiagramManager;
    Mouse/Touch Events are handled by the class DrawingPanel;
    at the top of the Canvas there is a menuBar (optional) with three menus (each optional); one menu each for choosing the format of displaying calculations (decimal number or fraction) and the width of the edges (see classes Vertex and Edge); via the third menu labels can be added/removed from the vertices, and an additional source (root) can be added to the flow diagram;
    at the bottom of the Canvas is an (optional) panel containing two buttons to refresh (new diagram) or undo changes in the flow diagram;
    this class reads the launchdata and takes care of getState/setState (see classes NoSer, Vertexcopy, EdgeCopy, DiagramCopy and DiagramCopier)
    StroomDiagrammenGWTClientBundle
    interface for the client bundle
    StroomDiagrammenGWTCssResource
    interface for cascading style sheets
    Vertex
    class representing a vertex in the flow diagram;
    each vertex has a flow, calculated from the flow entered in the root(s) to which the vertex is connected;
    edges out of the vertex are added by pressing the right arrow button and end in a new vertex;
    the flow in a vertex, which is not a root, can be traced back by pressing the left arrow button;
    vertices can be moved vertically in the same layer or horizontally when possible; putting two vertices on top of each other fuses them into one vertex; if a vertex is a terminal vertex (no outgoing edges) it can be deleted by dragging it onto the border of the work area (this also deletes its incoming edges)
    Mouse/Touch action on vertices is handled in class DrawingPanel;
    the initial flow in a root can be entered/changed by a doubleClick or longClick on the root, see also class VertexPopup;
    the layout of the flow diagram is controlled by the class DiagramManager;
    vertices can have a label: additional text in a rectangle above the vertex; text for the label is entered/changed by a doubleClick or longClick on the label, see also class VertexPopup.
    VertexCopy
    class containing basic attributes of a vertex
